title: The origins of cinema
titleCn: 电影起源：19世纪活动影像发明史
articleHtml:
The 19th-century inventions which led to the birth of the movies

 

A 

Many consider that the history of motion pictures began in 1824. Over the next decades, a British inventor William George Horner invented Zoetrope. Horner's device consisted of a hollow drum, rotated by means of a crank. Around the drum's inner surface was a strip of paper with a sequence of paintings, drawings, or illustrations on it. As the device turned, the viewer could observe the illusion of moving images through regularly spaced narrow slits.

 

B 

In 1861, the US inventor Coleman Sellers patented the Kinetatoscope, a device containing a sequence of stereoscopic (3D) photos on glass plates. 1870 saw the first public demonstrations of US inventor Henry Renno Heyl's Phasmatrope, one of the earliest devices to show apparently 'moving' photographs. On February 5th of that year, Heyl delighted audiences at the Academy of Music in Philadelphia with his photographs of dancers, shown in rapid succession so as to create the impression of motion.

 

C 

Devised in 1877 by Frenchman Charles Emile Reynaud, this refined version of the Zoetrope had mirrors at the centre of the drum. This was followed in 1879 by the British photographer Eadweard Muybridge's invention of the Zoopraxiscope. Images appeared on a screen, having been projected from a series of photos printed on a disc that turned when the machine was operating.

 

D 

However, true motion pictures, rather than eye-fooling 'animations', could only occur after French innovator and physiologist Etienne-Jules Marey, often constructing a camera that could take 12 photographs per second. Marey's chronophotographs, as he called them, were revolutionary, and he was soon able to achieve a rate of 30 images per second.

 

E 

In November 1890, William Dickson, devised a simple but ingenious motor-powered motion-picture camera known as the Kinetograph. Although its bulky motor was soon to be replaced with a lightweight hand-crank mechanism, the Kinetograph set the standard for the motion picture cameras that would be used for the next century.

 

F 

Dickson also designed an early version of a movie-picture projector called the Kinetoscope. Around that same time, he filmed his first experimental Kinetoscope trial film, Monkeyshines No. 1, the only surviving film from the cylinder Kinetoscope.

 

G 

Meanwhile in Lyons, France, brothers Louis and Auguste Lumière were inspired by Edison and Dickson's work. They created their own multi-purpose device, which combined camera, printer, and projecting capabilities, was more profitable than Edison and Dickson's model, because a number of spectators could watch the film on a large screen at the same time. On December 28, 1895, the Lumières presented the first commercial exhibition of a projected motion picture to a paying public in the world's first movie theatre in the Salon Indien.
